title: Map implementation requirements for multi-department university cohorts
description: Research how universities coordinate multiple departments, course leads and concurrent cohorts when adopting a shared learning workspace. Use public procurement and programme information plus consented interviews if approved. Verify every proposed workflow against the current Zedu product; deliver a rollout checklist, stakeholder map and list of unresolved requirements without implying unverified institutional features.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Map university adoption constraints from official programme and procurement evidence
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Review a bounded set of public university programme and procurement documents and code only explicit requirements for concurrent cohorts, department ownership, identity, accessibility, data handling, integrations and procurement. Cite each source and date, separate stated requirements from hypotheses, then compare them with Zedu workflows verified in the product or public documentation. Deliver a stakeholder map, evidence table, rollout checklist and unresolved questions; do not imply institutional demand or contact anyone.

Official programme/procurement evidence with explicit-versus-inferred coding is a defensible way to map departmental ownership and concurrent-cohort adoption constraints. The stakeholder map and unresolved requirements connect the research to an actionable rollout rather than implying universities are already customers. Reuse existing accreditation/integration research where applicable; concentrate new work on cross-department responsibilities and handoffs. Product/documentation checks must distinguish a published capability from behaviour actually tested, and institutional demand remains unproven.
Official programme and procurement documents are the only reliable evidence of what a university will require before it buys.

tasks.title: Map three universities department handoffs and rollout requirements against checked Zedu evidence

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Model a three-department pilot workspace and verify it works in a test org
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Turn the requirements into a concrete setup a university can copy. Approach: design the structure for three departments running concurrent cohorts (workspace vs. channel boundaries, naming, who is admin per department, how shared announcements reach all three, how files stay in their department), build it in a test workspace with synthetic accounts, and record every place the current product can't express the requirement. Done: the setup diagram, screenshots of the working test org, and a gap list for the product team.

That is useful validation rather than assuming a diagram proves product capability. Derive the three-department scenarios from the same requirements table, and use only the dedicated test org/account-holder authorization already being arranged under the test-workspace goal. Record a product gap when departmental isolation or role granularity cannot be expressed; do not imply those controls exist. Keep the result a demonstration and gap list, not a claimed university deployment or demand signal.
